newsitem.title: SWITZERLAND: SNB's Roth pleased with Swiss franc development.
newsitem.headline: SNB's Roth pleased with Swiss franc development.

text.p: Swiss National Bank (SNB) board member Jean-Pierre Roth said the central bank was pleased with recent developments in the Swiss franc's exchange rate and said the currency was now more realistically valued.
Roth also said the SNB was continuing its easy monetary policy that has been in effect since August.
"We still have the same strategy," Roth told reporters as he entered the Bank for International Settlements for a meeting of G10 central bank governors.

Roth noted the exchange rate policy was for a flexible Swiss franc. "The Swiss franc is flexible so we have had a strong Swiss franc and now have a correction of this strength, and it is becoming more realistic," he said.
The mark approached the key level of 80 Swiss centimes this summer but has since strengthened to above 85 centimes.
Roth said the SNB was pleased the franc had come down from levels that he described as unrealistic.
"It (the franc) was strong but not very realistic at that time so, we are pleased with developments," he said.
